subject: oop
text: Which constructor is called first for a derived class object?
explanation: Base construction happens first so the derived part builds on an initialised base.

subject: oop
text: Which access specifier makes members visible to derived classes but not outside the class?
explanation: protected allows derived-class access while still hiding members from unrelated code.
objective: protected allows derived-class access while still hiding members from unrelated code.

subject: oop
text: What is a friend function and why does it weaken encapsulation?
explanation: A friend is granted access to private and protected members, which bypasses the public interface.
objective: A friend is granted access to private and protected members, which bypasses the public interface.

subject: oop
text: What does the `override` keyword tell the compiler?
options: This function overrides a virtual base function
explanation: override makes the compiler verify a base virtual with the same signature exists.
objective: override makes the compiler verify a base virtual with the same signature exists.

subject: oop
text: Why must a base class destructor be virtual when deleting through a base pointer?
explanation: Without a virtual destructor only the base destructor runs, leaking derived resources.
objective: Without a virtual destructor only the base destructor runs, leaking derived resources.

subject: oop
text: What problem does the Observer pattern solve?
explanation: It defines a one-to-many dependency so dependents are notified without the subject knowing them.
